runs.text: The term ‘Nuristani’ refers to the people living in the remote Nuristan province of northeastern Afghanistan and the northern regions of Pakistan. They speak various languages from the Nuristani language group. Ethnically, the Nuristani people cluster embraces eight groups – the Ashkuni-Wamayi, Narisati, Grangali, Kamviri, Malakhel, Waigeli, Prasuni, and Tregami.

Initial contact between Christian workers and the people of Nuristan occurred indirectly. At that time, Nuristan was known as Kafiristan (land of the Kafirs). Kafirs meaning non-Muslim. Contact came through the British colonial army, particularly the Corps of Guides. Among its recruits, in Peshawar, were individuals from Kafiristan who had exposure to Christian teachings while serving in the army.

A Kafir soldier who showed interest in learning more about Christianity urged the Christian workers to visit his homeland in Kafiristan. In 1864, two Pashtun converts to Christianity, acting on an invitation from Kafir soldiers, made the first recorded mission journey to Kafiristan. Their mission involved Christian teaching, distributing translated scripture (in a trade language) and providing medical assistance to local communities. They were received positively. On their departure, a letter was sent by the local people requesting they return with further teachings. They were unable to return. There are records of others visiting Kafiristan during the following decades, but in 1896 the population was forcibly converted to Islam and Kafiristan was renamed Nuristan, ‘land of

Due to the political situation and the geographical location of Nuristan it is very difficult to access this remote region. In recent decades, Christian workers have brought medical teams to Nuristan, some lost their lives and others suffered great trauma. Due to the current security situation, it is no longer possible for foreigners to travel to this region of Afghanistan.

Nuristani people primarily live as farmers and herders. Men work in livestock herding while women work on grain production or irrigated terraces. Pray that soon they will hear the news that there is a good shepherd who loves and cares for them.
